levels.title: Foundations
levels.summary: The Python, API, SQL and tooling skills every later level assumes.

modules.title: Python for AI engineering
modules.scope: Modern Python setup (uv or venv + pip), type hints, dataclasses and Pydantic v2 models, f-strings, list/dict comprehensions, exceptions, context managers, reading/writing JSON and files, async/await basics with asyncio and httpx, pytest basics. Aimed at someone who has written a little code (any language).

modules.title: Web APIs, HTTP and JSON
modules.scope: HTTP methods, status codes, headers, JSON, REST conventions, API keys and auth headers, environment variables for secrets, rate limits and retries with backoff, pagination; calling APIs with httpx/requests; building a small API with FastAPI (routes, Pydantic request/response models, automatic docs).

modules.title: Just enough SQL
modules.scope: Tables and types, SELECT/WHERE/ORDER BY/LIMIT, INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, joins, GROUP BY and aggregates, UNIQUE constraints and upserts (ON CONFLICT) for idempotent writes, transactions, placeholders and SQL injection, indexes and EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN, full-text search (SQLite FTS5, Postgres) at a basic level; using SQLite from Python with sqlite3. Prepares for pgvector, memory stores, checkpointers and audit logs later.

modules.title: Git, the command line and Docker
modules.scope: Shell basics, git (commit, branch, merge, pull requests), GitHub, .gitignore and never committing secrets, Docker images/containers/Dockerfile/compose basics, GitHub Actions for running tests on push, writing a good README.

modules.title: Just enough machine learning
modules.scope: What a model is, training vs inference, neural networks and gradient descent at an intuitive level, supervised vs self-supervised learning, overfitting, embeddings as vectors of meaning, what a transformer is at a very high level. Visual/intuitive resources (3Blue1Brown, fast.ai, Google ML crash course). No heavy math required.

levels.title: LLM fundamentals
levels.summary: How large language models work and how to use them reliably from code.

modules.title: How LLMs work
modules.scope: Tokens and tokenization, next-token prediction, transformers and attention (intuition), pretraining vs instruction tuning vs RLHF, context windows, sampling (temperature, top-p), why models hallucinate, reasoning/thinking models at a high level, knowledge cutoffs.

modules.title: Calling LLM APIs
modules.scope: Using provider SDKs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini) and local open models (Ollama), the messages format (system/user/assistant), streaming responses, token counting and cost, rate limits and retries, choosing a model (capability vs cost vs latency), reasoning effort or thinking-budget settings and reasoning-token cost, multimodal input basics, keeping API keys safe.

modules.title: Prompt engineering
modules.scope: Clear instructions, roles/system prompts, few-shot examples, delimiters/XML tags, chain-of-thought and letting the model think, prompt templates and versioning, prompt chaining, common mistakes; official guides from Anthropic, OpenAI and Google; treating prompts as code that you test.

modules.title: Structured outputs and function calling basics
modules.scope: Getting reliable JSON: JSON Schema, provider structured-output modes, Pydantic validation, the Instructor library, retry-on-validation-error, function/tool calling as structured output, extraction and classification tasks.

modules.title: Your first evals
modules.scope: Why you must measure LLM output, building a small golden dataset, assertion-based checks, exact-match vs fuzzy vs LLM-graded checks (intro), tracking results across prompt versions, tools like promptfoo or a pytest-based harness. Keep it introductory; Level 5 goes deep.

levels.title: Retrieval and RAG
levels.summary: Grounding model answers in your own data with search, retrieval and citations.

modules.title: Embeddings and vector search
modules.scope: What embeddings are, embedding models and the MTEB leaderboard, cosine similarity, vector databases and indexes (HNSW, IVF) at a conceptual level, pgvector, Chroma, Qdrant, FAISS; choosing one; metadata filtering.

modules.title: Building a RAG pipeline
modules.scope: The RAG architecture end to end: loading and parsing documents (PDF, HTML), chunking strategies, indexing, retrieval, prompt assembly, citations and refusing when the answer isn't in the context; frameworks (LlamaIndex, LangChain) vs plain code; RAG vs long context vs fine-tuning.

modules.title: Better retrieval: hybrid search and reranking
modules.scope: Keyword search and BM25, hybrid search with reciprocal rank fusion, rerankers (cross-encoders, Cohere Rerank, open rerankers), query rewriting and HyDE, contextual retrieval (Anthropic), parent/child chunks, multi-hop questions.

modules.title: Evaluating RAG
modules.scope: Separating retrieval quality from generation quality, recall@k, MRR, nDCG, faithfulness/groundedness and answer relevance, building a question set from your corpus, Ragas and similar tools, error analysis on failures.

modules.title: Knowledge graphs and GraphRAG
modules.scope: When graph-structured retrieval helps (global questions, entity relationships), Microsoft GraphRAG, LightRAG-style approaches, Neo4j basics, cost trade-offs. Optional specialisation.

levels.title: Tools and agents
levels.summary: Letting models take actions: tool calling, the agent loop, workflow patterns, MCP and memory.

modules.title: Tool calling in depth
modules.scope: How tool/function calling works across providers, designing tool names/descriptions/schemas the model uses well, parallel tool calls, returning errors to the model, tool results size, idempotency for tools with side effects, security of tool inputs.

modules.title: The agent loop
modules.scope: What an agent is (model + tools + loop), ReAct, building an agent from scratch without a framework, stop conditions, max steps and token/cost budgets, error recovery, planning vs reacting, reflection, reasoning models in the loop (returning reasoning blocks with tool results, effort settings), when an agent is the wrong choice.

modules.title: Workflows and agent design patterns
modules.scope: Workflows vs agents; prompt chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer (Anthropic's Building effective agents); plan-and-execute; choosing the simplest pattern that works; agent design guides from OpenAI and Google.

modules.title: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
modules.scope: What MCP is and why it exists, hosts/clients/servers, tools/resources/prompts, transports (stdio, Streamable HTTP), building a server with the official Python SDK or FastMCP, connecting it to a client (Claude Desktop, an IDE, your own agent), authorization for remote servers, security risks of third-party servers.

modules.title: Memory and context engineering
modules.scope: Short-term vs long-term memory, conversation history management and summarisation, semantic/episodic/procedural memory, memory stores (Mem0, LangGraph store, Letta/MemGPT ideas), context engineering: what goes into the window and why, context rot and compaction, Agent Skills and progressive disclosure.

levels.title: Frameworks and multi-agent systems
levels.summary: Stateful agent frameworks, multi-agent designs, human approval and specialised agents.

modules.title: Stateful agents with LangGraph
modules.scope: Graphs, state, nodes and edges, conditional routing, checkpointers and persistence, interrupts and resuming, streaming, the LangChain Academy course; when a graph framework helps and when it's overhead.

modules.title: Agent SDKs compared
modules.scope: OpenAI Agents SDK, Claude Agent SDK, Google Agent Development Kit (ADK), Pydantic AI, CrewAI, Microsoft Agent Framework (AutoGen is in maintenance mode); what each abstracts, how to compare them, and building the same small agent in two of them.

modules.title: Multi-agent systems
modules.scope: Supervisor/orchestrator-worker, handoffs, swarms, debate; shared state vs message passing; Anthropic's multi-agent research system lessons (token cost); when not to go multi-agent (Cognition's 'Don't build multi-agents'); A2A protocol for agents from different vendors.

modules.title: Human in the loop
modules.scope: Deciding which actions need approval, pausing and resuming durable runs, approval UIs, editing proposed actions, audit trails, undo/rollback, confidence-based escalation.

modules.title: Coding agents
modules.scope: How coding agents work (tools: read/search/edit/run tests), sandboxing code execution, repository instructions (AGENTS.md), harnesses for long-running work, SWE-bench; using and building one. Optional specialisation.

modules.title: Browser and computer-use agents
modules.scope: Observing pages via DOM/accessibility tree vs screenshots, Playwright, browser-use library, Playwright MCP, computer-use tools from providers, reliability and safety (credentials, prompt injection from web pages), evaluation (WebArena, OSWorld). Optional specialisation.

levels.title: Evaluation, observability and safety
levels.summary: Measuring agent quality, seeing what agents do in production and defending them against attack.

modules.title: Evals in depth
modules.scope: Error analysis first (look at your data), eval-driven development, LLM-as-a-judge done right (calibrating against human labels), trajectory and tool-use evals for agents, regression evals in CI, eval tools (Inspect AI, promptfoo, DeepEval, OpenAI Evals, Braintrust/LangSmith datasets). Hamel Husain, Eugene Yan, Shreya Shankar writing.

modules.title: Observability and tracing
modules.scope: Tracing LLM and agent runs, spans for model calls and tools, OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions, open-source and hosted tools (Langfuse, Arize Phoenix, LangSmith, OpenLLMetry), token/cost/latency dashboards, online quality signals and user feedback.

modules.title: Security and guardrails
modules.scope: Prompt injection (direct and indirect), the lethal trifecta, OWASP Top 10 for LLM applications and for agentic applications, least-privilege tools, sandboxing, PII handling, jailbreaks, guardrail tools (e.g. Guardrails AI, NeMo Guardrails, Llama Guard), red-teaming (garak, PyRIT), design patterns for securing agents.

modules.title: Reading agent benchmarks
modules.scope: What SWE-bench (Verified), tau-bench, GAIA, WebArena, OSWorld, Terminal-Bench measure; pass@k vs pass^k; contamination and leaderboard pitfalls; reading a model launch claim critically. Optional.

project.title: Harden an agent: evals, tracing and red-teaming

levels.title: Production and scale
levels.summary: Deploying, scaling and operating agents reliably and affordably.

modules.title: Deploying agent applications
modules.scope: Serving with FastAPI and streaming (SSE), background jobs and queues, durable execution for long-running agents (Temporal, LangGraph persistence, Inngest/Restate-style), containers, serverless vs Kubernetes, configuration and secrets, CI/CD with an eval gate, canary releases for prompt/model changes.

modules.title: Reliability, latency and cost
modules.scope: LLM gateways (LiteLLM, cloud gateways), fallbacks across providers, timeouts and retries, rate limits and per-user budgets, prompt caching, semantic caching, batching, model routing and smaller models, measuring cost per task.

modules.title: Agent system design and capacity planning
modules.scope: Decision briefs (baseline, autonomy boundary, systems of record, non-goals, kill criterion), SLIs and SLOs from user outcomes, system planes and state ownership, Little's law and provider quotas, latency budgets, cost per useful task and sensitivity, vector storage and rebuild time, serving memory (weights plus KV cache), human review capacity, architecture decision records. Companion worked examples from the Agentic AI Mastery guide. Optional.

modules.title: Open models, fine-tuning and serving
modules.scope: When to fine-tune vs prompt vs RAG, LoRA/QLoRA, the Hugging Face ecosystem (Transformers, PEFT, TRL), distillation for agents, reinforcement fine-tuning (GRPO) at a high level, serving open models with vLLM or Ollama, quantization. Optional specialisation.

modules.title: Staying current and building a portfolio
modules.scope: How to read papers (arXiv, Papers with Code alternatives), newsletters and blogs worth following, writing technical posts, demo videos, contributing to open-source agent projects, preparing for AI engineering interviews (system design for LLM apps).

interview.title: Agentic AI interview prep
interview.summary: Turn what you built into interview answers: agentic system design, a question bank, product, evaluation, coding and enterprise rounds, behavioural stories and timed mocks.

pages.title: How to prepare
pages.scope: What AI engineering interview loops look like, which guide levels each round draws on, a six-week plan and a two-week sprint, the evidence pack to bring, readiness checks.

pages.title: Agentic system design rounds
pages.scope: What the round tests, a 45-minute timeline, a six-step answer structure, three worked prompts (support agent with refunds, permission-aware knowledge assistant, long-running research with specialists), follow-up probes, strong and weak signals.

pages.title: Question bank
pages.scope: Around 40 common questions with short model answers and a follow-up for each, grouped into LLM fundamentals (including attention, KV cache, prefill and decode, quantization, constrained decoding and tuning methods), agents and tools, state and approvals, retrieval, context and security, and evaluation and operations.

pages.title: AI product and customer rounds
pages.scope: The customer or product-manager simulation round: leading a scoping conversation, questions that change the design, deciding whether an LLM fits, outcome, quality, guardrail and cost metrics, a first release and pilot, a worked support-team example, common traps.

pages.title: Evaluation and debugging rounds
pages.scope: Worked judge calibration (TPR, TNR, correcting a judge-estimated rate), confidence intervals and paired comparisons on small eval sets, pass^k, designing an eval for a new tool, a six-step debugging method and five worked agent failures (tool-call loops, retrieval drift after a rebuild, model upgrade regressions, cost spikes, unfaithful answers).

pages.title: Coding and debugging rounds
pages.scope: What agent coding rounds look like, a contract-first method, warm-ups, six runtime problems with acceptance checks, a trace-debugging round with common bugs, and how attempts are scored.

pages.title: Enterprise and regulated settings
pages.scope: Governance and model-risk questions for banks and other regulated companies: frameworks by name (NIST AI RMF and its generative AI profile, US SR 26-2, RBI FREE-AI, OWASP), launch approval, personal data with hosted models, audit trails, explainability, bias testing, vendor model changes, data residency, agent actions on accounts, monitoring and vendor due diligence.

pages.title: Behavioural and leadership stories
pages.scope: What the round tests, STAR plus reflection, a story bank mapped to common questions, making stories verifiable, using guide projects honestly, senior and leadership scenarios, questions to ask interviewers.

pages.title: Mock interviews and scoring
pages.scope: Five timed mock rounds (system design, coding, incident, evaluation review, customer conversation) with prompts, a six-dimension scoring rubric, how to run mocks alone or with a peer, the retake loop and a readiness gate.
